paper_title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is central to improving long-CoT reasoning in large language models. Critic-free methods such as GRPO convert response-level rewards into advantages and uniformly broadcast them across tokens, overlooking their unequal contributions to the final outcome. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) instead provides dense distributional supervision by minimizing the forward KL divergence between an unprivileged policy and a privileged self-teacher, implicitly assuming that the resulting likelihood shifts encode reliable answer-aligned information. We test this premise by fixing each sampled trajectory and re-scoring it under two opposing outcome conditions, one asserting correctness and the other incorrectness. Most affected tokens shift in the same direction under both conditions, with few sign reversals and substantial overlap in the induced optimization signals. Large shifts also concentrate on highly substitutable surface-form tokens, whereas tokens carrying problem-specific reasoning content are less sensitive. These findings show that privileged shifts fail to provide reliable answer-aligned directions, while their magnitudes primarily reflect counterfactual sensitivity rather than token-level learning value. Based on these observations, we propose Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation (CSCR), a simple extension of GRPO that reduces credit for highly sensitive tokens and renormalizes token-level advantages to preserve both the original credit budget and verifier-determined direction. On long-CoT mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CSCR consistently outperforms GRPO baseline with the same number of policy updates. Targeted ablations further corroborate our diagnosis: privilege-induced directions are unreliable, moderate downweighting is most effective, and stronger modulation destabilizes optimization.

sections.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is central to improving long-CoT reasoning in large language models. Large shifts also concentrate on highly substitutable surface-form tokens, whereas tokens carrying problem-specific reasoning content are less sensitive. On long-CoT mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CSCR consistently outperforms GRPO baseline with the same number of policy updates. Targeted ablations further corroborate our diagnosis: privilege-induced directions are unreliable, moderate downweighting is most effective, and stronger modulation destabilizes optimization. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as powerful post-training paradigm for improving large language models in domains such as mathematics and code, where final outcomes can be evaluated automatically and at scale Shao et al. (2024); Lambert et al. (2024); Guo et al. (2025); Yu et al. (2026); Hu et al. (2026); Wen et al. (2025). Critic-free methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and its recent variants estimate relative advantages from groups of sampled responses and uniformly broadcast each sequence-level advantage across all generated tokens, avoiding learned value models and costly process-level annotation Shao et al. (2024); Liu et al. (2025); Yu et al. (2026). This simplicity has enabled scalable long-CoT training, but also creates fundamental mismatch between outcome-level evaluation and token-level optimization: within response spanning thousands of tokens, decisive reasoning steps, exploratory branches, and largely prefix-determined continuations receive identical credit despite contributing differently to the final outcome Kazemnejad et al. (2024); Parthasarathi et al. (2025); Tan et al. (2025). Process-supervision approaches seek to address this mismatch by assigning denser intermediate feedback, but typically rely on step-level annotations, auxiliary reward models, or additional rollouts Lightman et al. (2024); Luo et al. (2024). Developing reliable and scalable token-level credit signals while retaining the simplicity of outcome-supervised RLVR therefore remains central challenge for long-CoT reasoning. On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level distributional supervision by querying teacher on studentgenerated trajectories under the same prefixes, thereby reducing the traininference distribution mismatch inherent in off-policy distillation Gu et al. (2024); Agarwal et al. (2024); Ko et al. (2024); Jin et al. (2026). However, standard OPD is not naturally aligned with RLVR, since teacher likelihoods reflect the teachers own distribution rather than verifier correctness and may therefore reinforce incorrect trajectories or suppress valid student solutions Zheng et al. (2026). Its effectiveness 1 Figure 1: Counterfactual likelihood-shift statistics across model scales, computed from 400 on-policy trajectories generated for 100 questions sampled from DAPO-17K, with four trajectories per question, using 𝜆 = 0.05. (a) Proportions of tokens significant under both, exactly one, or neither privileged condition. (b) Proportions of jointly significant tokens with same-sign or opposite-sign shifts. also depends strongly on teacherstudent compatibility: even stronger teacher may provide ineffective supervision when its reasoning patterns diverge from those of the student Li et al. (2026b). Moreover, evaluating separate teacher over every student-generated trajectory incurs substantial computational and memory overhead, especially for long-form reasoning Li et al. (2026b); Yang et al. (2026c). These limitations have motivated on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), where the policy itself serves as privileged teacher conditioned on verified answers, reference solutions, or outcome feedback, and transfers its conditional distribution to the unprivileged branch through KL optimization Zhao et al. (2026a); Penaloza et al. (2026). Recent studies have extended this paradigm through feedback-conditioned self-teaching Hübotter et al. (2026), hybrid RLdistillation objectives and adaptive routing Li et al. (2026a), verifier-aligned or outcome-guided calibration of the self-teacher Yang et al. (2026a,b), and contrastive, reflective, or error-focused supervision Pan et al. (2026); Zhao et al. (2026b). sections.title: 3 Method
sections.content: Building on the preceding analysis, CSCR uses counterfactual sensitivity to reallocate GRPO credit across tokens. Tokens with higher sensitivity receive smaller token-level weights, while the verifier-derived sequence advantage continues to determine the optimization direction. The resulting weights are renormalized to preserve the credit budget.

sections.title: 4.1 Experimental Setup
sections.content: Datasets. We use DAPO-17K Yu et al. (2026) as the training dataset, which contains challenging mathematical reasoning problems designed for long-CoT reinforcement learning. We evaluate all methods on five held-out competition-level benchmarks: AMC23 MAA and Math-AI (2023), AIME24 Zhang and Math-AI (2024), AIME25 Zhang and Math-AI (2025), AIME26 Zhang and Math-AI (2026), and SMT-2025 Dekoninck et al. (2026). These benchmarks cover varying levels of mathematical difficulty and enable more comprehensive evaluation of overall reasoning performance and robustness on challenging problems. Baselines. We compare CSCR with GRPO Shao et al. (2024) and five self-distillation methods. OPSD Zhao et al. (2026a) distills the token distributions of privileged self-teacher along onpolicy rollouts. SDPO Hübotter et al. (2026) converts feedbackconditioned self-teacher predictions into dense token-level supervision. SRPO Li et al. (2026a) routes correct rollouts to GRPO and incorrect rollouts to SDPO, with entropy-aware weighting applied to the distillation branch. RLSD Yang et al. (2026a) uses verifier-derived advantages for update directions and privileged likelihood differences to modulate token-level credit magnitudes. RLCSD Pan et al. (2026) contrasts correct and incorrect student rollouts to isolate task-relevant privileged shifts and uses the contrastive signal for token-level credit modulation. Implementation Details. We conduct experiments on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B Yang et al. (2025) using fullparameter fine-tuning with the veRL Sheng et al. (2025) framework on eight NVIDIA H800 GPUs. All methods use learning rate of 2 106 throughout all experiments and are trained for 300 steps. sections.title: 4.2 Main Results
sections.content: Overall Performance. Table 4 shows that CSCR achieves the best result across all ten modelbenchmark combinations, outperforming GRPO and all five self-distillation baselines despite being minimal modification of GRPO. Compared with the strongest competing method on each benchmark, CSCR improves performance by an average of 3.9 points on Qwen31.7B and 1.7 points on Qwen3-4B. Several self-distillation methods even underperform the base model on multiple benchmarks, consistent with our diagnosis that overemphasizing large privilege-induced likelihood shifts can hinder policy optimization. In contrast, attenuating counterfactually sensitive tokens 6 suggests that mild attenuation suppresses sensitivity-driven noise while preserving enough credit on these positions to maintain stable autoregressive transitions. By contrast, downweighting with 𝛾 {0.5, 1.0} collapses: reward approaches zero, entropy spikes before collapsing, and response length falls to approximately 6,000 and 2,000 tokens, respectively. Under within-trajectory normalization, excessive attenuation nearly suppresses sensitive tokens while concentrating redistributed credit on the remaining positions, thereby distorting the balance required for coherent long-form reasoning. Since sensitive tokens, although less informative, still support coherent autoregressive generation, this overcorrection destabilizes optimization. Overall, sensitive tokens should be moderately downweighted rather than emphasized or nearly ignored.

sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: We investigate whether privileged likelihood shifts provide reliable token-level supervision for long-CoT RLVR. Across 400 on-policy trajectories, our analysis separates shift direction from magnitude at both sampled-token and full-vocabulary levels under fixed prefixes. Counterfactual re-scoring shows that opposing outcome conditions induce predominantly samedirection shifts and substantially overlapping forward-KL signals, while large shifts concentrate on substitutable surfaceform tokens rather than problem-specific reasoning content. We therefore reinterpret shift magnitude as counterfactual sensitivity and propose CSCR, minimal GRPO extension that preserves verifier-derived direction and trajectory-level credit while reallocating credit away from highly sensitive tokens. CSCR consistently outperforms GRPO and all self-distillation baselines across both model scales and all five benchmarks. Ablations further show that trusting shift signs causes rapid optimization collapse, moderate downweighting yields the strongest and most stable gains, and stronger modulation in either direction destabilizes optimization. These results challenge privileged distributional changes as direct supervision and establish counterfactual sensitivity as practical basis for reliable token-level credit reallocation. yields consistent gains across both model scales and all five benchmarks. Training Dynamics. Figure 3 compares the training trajectories of GRPO and CSCR on Qwen3-1.7B. CSCR separates from GRPO early and maintains higher smoothed reward throughout training, indicating sustained optimization advantage. Its average response length increases gradually from approximately 10,000 to 11,500 tokens before stabilizing, while GRPO remains near 9,50010,000 tokens. This increase stays well below the 20,480-token limit and shows neither length explosion nor reward collapse, demonstrating stable optimization with moderately longer reasoning.

sections.title: 4.3 Ablation Studies
sections.content: Reliability of Privileged Shift Directions. To test whether the sign of privileged likelihood shift provides reliable optimization direction, we construct Shift-Directed GRPO (SD-GRPO) as minimal intervention on GRPO. Using the ground-truth answer as privileged information, we compute the token shift 𝑧𝑖,𝑡 and assume that tokens with the largest absolute shifts may carry directional information. For tokens satisfying 𝑧𝑖,𝑡 > 𝜆, we replace the verifier-derived advantage 𝐴𝑖 with sign(𝑧𝑖,𝑡 ) 𝐴𝑖 , while leaving all others unchanged. We evaluate 𝜆 {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} to test whether trusting small subset of highly shifted tokens can improve optimization. Figure 4 shows that 𝜆 = 0.2, 0.1, and 0.05 reverse the GRPO advantage sign for approximately 1.5%, 3%, and 5% of tokens, respectively. Nevertheless, all variants collapse within about 30 updates: the training reward falls from roughly 0.8 to zero, entropy approaches zero, and response length reaches the 20,480-token limit. Inspection of the resulting generations reveals persistent repetition of tokens such as the and but. As shown in Table 3, these highly shifted surface-form tokens receive positive shifts far more often than negative ones under privileged conditioning, causing SD-GRPO to reinforce them disproportionately. Representative cases are provided in Appendix E. These results show that even the directions of the largest privileged shifts are unreliable for token-level credit assignment. Upweighting versus Downweighting Sensitive Tokens. To determine whether counterfactually sensitive tokens should receive more or less credit, we compare CSCR-UpWeight and CSCR-DownWeight under the same sensitivity score, threshold, and within-trajectory normalization. For tokens above the sensitivity threshold, the former increases their raw weights toward 1 + 𝛾, whereas the latter decreases them toward 1 𝛾. We evaluate 𝛾 {0.2, 0.5, 1.0} to examine both the preferred credit direction and the effect of modulation strength. Figure 5 shows that moderate downweighting with 𝛾 = 0.2 provides the most stable optimization, achieving the highest training reward, steady validation gains, gradual response-length growth, and limited entropy variation. Upweighting with 𝛾 = 0.2 improves over GRPO, whereas stronger upweighting raises entropy from approximately 0.2 to 0.6 and 0.8 for 𝛾 = 0.5 and 1.0, respectively, and yields little validation improvement. sections.title: Privileged Prompts
sections.content: Large Shifts Predominantly Affect Surface-Form Tokens. Table B.1 shows consistent separation between tokens with large and near-zero likelihood shifts. Under both counterfactual privileged prompts, the large-shift lists are dominated by discourse markers, local transition cues, and other highly substitutable surface-form tokens, including But, So, Let, Wait, Therefore, and Maybe. By contrast, the near-zero lists are enriched with digits, variables, arithmetic operators, and mathematical notation, such as 09, =, +, -, /, and . Although neither category is semantically exclusive, the contrast is stable under both 𝑐pos and 𝑐neg: privileged conditioning primarily perturbs stylistic realization and discourse organization, while tokens encoding problem-specific calculations are substantially less sensitive. Sensitive Token Identities Are Stable across Counterfactual Prompts. The tokens most sensitive to the positive and negative privileged prompts exhibit substantial overlap. Among the Top-50 tokens with positive likelihood shifts, 47 appear under both 𝑧pos > 0.1 and 𝑧neg > 0.1, corresponding to Jaccard similarity of 47/53 = 88.7%. The Top-50 negative-shift lists exhibit the same overlap, sharing 47 tokens with Jaccard similarity of 88.7%. When the positive and negative tails are combined, the two privileged conditions contain 64 and 66 unique high-shift tokens, respectively, of which 61 are shared, yielding Jaccard similarity of 88.4%. The near-zero lists are even more consistent, sharing 49 of their Top-50 entries. These results indicate that reversing the semantic polarity of privileged conditioning changes the magnitude and ranking of individual shifts more than it changes which token types are sensitive. Positive and Negative Shifts Affect Largely Overlapping Token Classes. Positive and negative likelihood shifts also affect broadly similar token classes within each privileged condition. Under 𝑐pos, the Top-50 positiveand negative-shift lists account for 71,445 and 72,021 sampled-token occurrences, respectively, and share 36 token identities. Under 𝑐neg, the corresponding lists account for 115,771 and 102,072 occurrences and share 34 token identities. Thus, neither shift direction is confined to distinct semantic class: many of the same discourse markers and highly substitutable surface-form tokens occur frequently in both tails, with their signs varying across contexts and token positions. Although the relative frequencies differ more under 𝑐neg, the substantial identity overlap remains stable across both conditions. Robustness across Alternative Counterfactual Privileged Prompts C.1 Alternative Counterfactual Privileged

sections.title: Prompt Constructions
sections.content: To assess whether our findings depend on the deliberately polarized prompts used in the main text, we construct three additional pairs of counterfactual privileged prompts, summarized in Table C.1. For all constructions, we keep the problem, sampled trajectory, and every token prefix fixed, modifying only the additional privileged context used during likelihood re-scoring. Within each construction, the positive and negative conditions follow the same prompt template and differ only in the privileged information that determines their intended correctness polarity. The answer-level construction holds the ground-truth answer fixed and counterfactually describes the same answer as either correct or incorrect. It therefore isolates the effect of asserted answer-level correctness while controlling for the answer content itself. The mild outcome-only construction states only whether the sampled trajectory reaches the correct final answer, without revealing the answer, providing reference solution, identifying specific error, or explicitly evaluating the quality of the reasoning process. Compared with the polarized prompts used in the main text, this construction removes strongly evaluative language and retains only concise trajectory-level outcome feedback. Finally, the reference-solution construction provides either correct or an incorrect reasoning process through otherwise identical prompt templates. The correct and incorrect reference solutions are generated by DeepSeek-V4-Pro and subsequently reviewed manually to confirm that they satisfy their designated correctness labels. Together, these three constructions cover privileged information at the answer, trajectory-outcome, and full-reasoning levels. They allow us to determine whether the observed likelihoodshift patterns persist across substantially different forms and strengths of counterfactual conditioning, rather than arising specifically from the polarized wording adopted in the main experiments. Full-Vocabulary Shift Composition. Figure C.1 shows that same-sign shifts remain the dominant component under all three alternative prompt constructions and across all probability thresholds. Under answer-level counterfactual feedback, jointly significant same-sign shifts account for 72.2%76.3% of the entries significant under the positive privileged condition, whereas opposite-sign shifts account for only 10.5%13.6%. The dominance is even stronger under mild outcome-only feedback: same-sign shifts constitute 88.9%92.2% of the reference set, while only 4.9%5.8% reverse direction. Thus, removing the strongly evaluative praise and criticism used in the main-text prompts does not reduce coordinate-wise directional agreement. Instead, the two opposing outcome conditions produce an even larger proportion of probability shifts pointing in the same direction. Reference-solution conditioning introduces the greatest content-level difference between the two privileged conditions, because the model receives complete correct or incorrect reasoning process. This construction produces larger proportion of opposite-sign shifts than the other alternatives, but samesign changes nevertheless remain predominant: they account for 63.7%65.3% of the reference set, compared with 19.1% 21.2% for opposite-sign changes. Even complete reasoning processes with opposing correctness polarity therefore fail to induce predominantly reversed coordinate-wise shift pattern. As 𝜖 increases, the same-sign proportion varies only moderately, while the fraction significant exclusively under the positive condition generally increases. Crucially, the opposite-sign proportion remains small or decreases rather than becoming dominant. The observed directional agreement is therefore not confined to weak perturbations near zero. Across answerlevel judgments, mild trajectory-level outcomes, and complete reference solutions, opposing privileged semantics primarily preserve common full-vocabulary update directions instead of reversing them. Rather than separating the cases by threshold, we present two representative examples from AIME24 in Table E.1. Inspection of all 30 AIME24 validation responses from the collapsed SD-GRPO runs reveals the same characteristic pattern: the generation eventually enters repetitive loop whose recurring span begins with The.
